market.summary: The feared gap-down did not hold: India closed at a nine-month high while Asia had its worst week since 2020, as foreign money rotated out of global AI/chip stocks and into Indian banks. Large caps led; midcaps rose a little but smallcaps slipped and more stocks fell than rose, and media was the weakest sector. For your holdings that means a supportive backdrop for the hotel and broker trades, a softer one for Tips Music, and little help for small caps like Bhageria.

points.text: Nifty Midcap 100 +0.66%, Smallcap 100 -0.13%; on BSE 2,456 stocks fell and 1,582 rose. Nifty Media about -2%, the worst sector of the day.
Foreign investors have put a record $12.21 bn into Indian equities so far in November; the rupee closed at 92.67 per dollar, a seven-month high, up 62 paise.
Asian markets had their worst week since March 2020 on AI and semiconductor selling (Japan, Korea, Taiwan weakest); India rose for a fourth straight week.
Brent near $90/bbl in the afternoon after reports of attacks on Saudi Arabia and tanker disruption near Hormuz; MCX gold -3.4%, silver -3.9%.

market.watch: Whether foreign buying continues next week while Asia stays weak; a reversal of that flow would hit large caps first, and crude above $90 is the risk to watch.

GROWW.summary: No new filing today. Groww closed ₹224.57, back above its 10 EMA (₹220.85) after Thursday's close just above it, on a day when financials led the market. This week's ₹1,905 Cr block where Ribbit Capital sold to long-only funds (BlackRock, Fidelity, Norges, Kotak MF, HDFC Life) was absorbed at ₹219, which supports the trade: a known seller's supply went into strong hands.

points.text: 17 Nov: Ribbit Capital's two entities sold about 8.7 crore shares (1.38% of the company) at ₹219, about ₹1,905 Cr; buyers included Kotak MF, BlackRock, Societe Generale, Fidelity, BNP Paribas, Morgan Stanley, HDFC Life and Norges Bank.
NSE's block-deal report shows BlackRock funds buying at least 65.5 lakh shares at ₹219 on 17 Nov.
Ribbit still held roughly 6.9% after this sale (8.29% in Sept less 1.38%), so more supply from it is possible later.

GROWW.watch: Trade is about +2R with the stop at cost: half goes on a close below ₹220.85 (10 EMA), the rest below ₹214.14 (20 EMA).

SEJALLTD.summary: Sejal bounced 5% to ₹922.95 today, back above your cost (₹884.13) and the 10 EMA (₹893.86), so the card shows TRAILING again. But Thursday's close of ₹877.95 was below cost, which under your rule was a full exit signal; if you still hold, you are holding past that signal. The news flow is supportive but small: the ₹40.80 Cr purchase of Magnumtuff's glass plant closes by 30 Nov.

points.text: Business transfer agreement signed 14 Nov: Sejal buys Magnumtuff India's architectural and automotive glass business (plant in Belgaum district, Karnataka, with brand, IP and staff) as a going concern for ₹40.80 Cr including land and building, closing on or before 30 Nov 2026.
The acquired unit had FY26 operating revenue of ₹36.20 Cr; the deal makes Sejal a four-plant manufacturer.
Closes since entry (exchange files): 870.35 on 16 Oct, 951.95 on 11 Nov (+1R), 877.95 on 19 Nov (below cost), 922.95 on 20 Nov.

SEJALLTD.watch: Your rule now: half below the 10 EMA (₹893.86), the rest on a close below cost ₹884.13. The deal's closing filing (by 30 Nov) is the next news.

THELEELA.summary: No new news. Leela closed ₹698.10, a new closing high, with seven accumulation days and no distribution days in the last 25 sessions. A risk-on day for large caps helped; the trade is about +3R with the stop at cost and ₹20 of room above the 10 EMA.

points.text: Last 25 sessions: 7 accumulation days, 0 distribution days, up/down volume 4.4x (engine's selling-pressure read).
Indian benchmarks rose for a fourth straight week to a nine-month high; realty +1.55%.

THELEELA.watch: Sell half on a close below ₹678.58 (10 EMA), the rest below ₹660.09 (20 EMA).

INDHOTEL.summary: No new filing beyond routine analyst-meet notices. Indian Hotels rose 2.5% to ₹912, a new closing high, closing near the top of the day's range on above-average volume. The trade is about +2.8R and the sell-half level (10 EMA ₹884.33) is now 3% below.

points.text: 20 Nov: high ₹913, low ₹882.90, close ₹912 on 44 lakh shares (vs 26 lakh the day before).
Healthcare, banks and realty led a broad large-cap rally; Sensex +1.08%.

INDHOTEL.watch: Sell half on a close below ₹884.33 (10 EMA), the rest below ₹858.49 (20 EMA).

TIPSMUSIC.summary: Tips slipped to ₹808.05, closing in the lower quarter of the day's range on light volume, while the Nifty Media index fell about 2% as the day's worst sector. It is now only 0.7% above its 10 EMA (₹802.74), so a weak Monday could trigger the sell-half signal. Today's filing is only a schedule of investor meetings (Kotak), no new information.

points.text: Nifty Media about -2% on 20 Nov, the weakest sector.
Filing 20 Nov: schedule of an institutional investor meeting arranged by Kotak (routine, no numbers).
Close ₹808.05 vs 10 EMA ₹802.74 and 20 EMA ₹783.45; the trade is about +1.2R with the stop at cost (₹727.89) or the 20 EMA, whichever is higher.

TIPSMUSIC.watch: A close below ₹802.74 sells half; below ₹783.45 (20 EMA) the rest.

BHAGERIA.summary: No new news found. Bhageria fell again to ₹344.05, below both your cost (₹367.46) and the original stop (₹360.01); it has closed below the stop since 16 Nov except one day. Smallcaps fell while large caps rallied, so the market is not helping. The plan's exit stands.

points.text: Nifty Smallcap 100 -0.13% and more stocks fell than rose on a day the Nifty gained 1.1%.

BHAGERIA.watch: Exit signalled; once sold, tell Claude the exit price so it is marked CLOSED.
